steps.title: Launch the Experiential Learning Community
steps.summary: Launch the Experiential Learning Community as the prototype for King's wider Strategic Communities of Practice model. Mobilise growing interest across faculties in developing more experiential and internship-like learning within the curriculum by connecting interested colleagues from faculties and professional services. Hold an informal pre-launch event in July, establish a dedicated Teams space for the emerging community, and formally launch it through an Unconference on 14 September 2026. Use the Unconference to share existing practice, form new connections, surface ideas and potential collaborations, begin a King's Taxonomy of Experiential Learning, and agree practical next steps and aspirations for the community's first year. Complete this prototype launch phase by the end of September 2026. The experience of forming the community, sustaining participation through Teams and translating the launch into collaborative activity will inform the common model used for subsequent communities.

outputs.title: Founding community mobilised
outputs.summary: A cross-institutional network of faculty and professional-services colleagues brought together through the July pre-launch, wider engagement and the September Unconference.
acceptanceCriteria: The July informal pre-launch event has taken place and helped identify the founding network.
At least 50 people participate in the Unconference, with representation from at least six faculties and multiple professional-services areas.
Careers and Employability and King's Academy contribute visibly to the launch.
Volunteers or prospective champions are identified to help carry activity forward.

outputs.title: Experiential Learning Unconference launch
outputs.summary: The Strategic Community of Practice formally launched on 14 September 2026 through a participatory Unconference focused on sharing practice, generating ideas, forming connections and identifying opportunities for collaboration.
acceptanceCriteria: The Unconference is delivered on 14 September 2026.
Participant-led discussions, examples and ideas are captured.
The purpose of the community and routes for continued involvement are made clear.
The event creates visible connections between colleagues with related interests and potential collaborations.

outputs.title: Experiential Learning SCoP Teams space
outputs.summary: A shared Teams space through which members can continue exchanging practice, developing ideas, forming collaborations and coordinating the community's activity, including colleagues unable to attend the launch.
acceptanceCriteria: The Teams space is provisioned before the Unconference and founding participants are invited.
At least 40 colleagues have joined by the end of September 2026.
Clear administration and moderation arrangements are in place.
Launch materials, the synthesis map and agreed next steps are published in the space.

outputs.title: Unconference synthesis map
outputs.summary: A visual synthesis of the practices, concepts, relationships and emerging opportunities surfaced during the day, forming the initial basis of a King's Taxonomy of Experiential Learning.
acceptanceCriteria: The principal forms of experiential and internship-like learning surfaced during the day are represented.
Existing examples, shared ideas and potential connections are captured.
Areas requiring further definition or development are identified.
The synthesis map is published through the Teams space.

outputs.title: First-year community next steps
outputs.summary: An initial set of actionable priorities, potential collaborations and aspirations agreed through the Unconference to guide the community's activity over the subsequent academic year.
acceptanceCriteria: At least three practical priorities or collaboration strands are identified.
Interested contributors or prospective champions are associated with each strand where possible.
Immediate next actions are recorded.
The next steps are shared and developed through the Teams space.

existingCapacity.contribution: Lead community mobilisation, design and convene the July pre-launch and September Unconference, coordinate contributors, and oversee synthesis and follow-through.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The launch would lack clear ownership, coherence and follow-through.

existingCapacity.role: Volunteer event, facilitation and community support
existingCapacity.owner: Careers and Employability and King's Academy
existingCapacity.contribution: Support event design, communications, participant engagement, facilitation, capture of outputs and establishment of the continuing community.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The event would place too much operational demand on the step lead and provide less effective facilitation, capture and follow-through.

existingCapacity.contribution: Contribute examples, ideas and expertise; participate in the Unconference; and help identify the community's priorities, collaboration opportunities and prospective champions.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The launch would not represent the breadth of institutional interest or establish a viable cross-institutional community.

newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before catering is commissioned for 14 September 2026
newInvestment.rationale: Provides a reasonable provisional envelope for refreshments and light catering for up to 100 participants, supporting an inclusive and hospitable participatory event.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The event can still proceed, but the participant experience, dwell time and opportunity for informal community formation may be reduced.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm a suitable venue and event arrangements for an Unconference of up to 100 participants on 14 September 2026.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The formal launch cannot proceed at the intended scale or in the intended participatory format.

enablingConditions.condition: Provision the Experiential Learning SCoP Teams space before the formal launch.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Colleagues unable to attend and participants seeking to continue the work would lack a shared route into the community.

enablingConditions.condition: Secure broad and timely promotion across faculties and professional services.
enablingConditions.owner: Mark Peace with Careers and Employability and King's Academy volunteers
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Attendance and institutional representation may be too narrow to form a credible founding community.

risks.title: Welcome Week timing reduces availability
risks.mitigation: Issue invitations and promotion early, use the July pre-launch to build commitment, and use the Teams space to enable colleagues who cannot attend to join the community, review the synthesis and contribute to next steps. The 14 September date remains preferable to moving into the teaching term or into the pre-holiday and conference period.

risks.title: The launch creates interest but not a continuing community
risks.mitigation: Use a participant-led Unconference format, agree practical next steps and collaboration strands during the event, identify prospective champions, and carry activity forward through the Teams space.

steps.title: Agree the SCoP Operating Model
steps.summary: By December 2026, agree the standard operating model for Strategic Communities of Practice. Define how communities are established and led, how they are resourced, what their funding may be used for, how decisions are made, how they are governed and held to account, and the minimum expectations for activity, outputs and institutional impact. Alongside this, develop an institutional proposition for workload release, workload allocation or backfill for community convenors and colleagues leading funded projects. Faculties will need to take a view on how this can operate consistently and fairly within their own workload and resource arrangements. Use evidence and learning from the Experiential Learning prototype while developing the model, and secure enough clarity to support the first funded convenor and community-project calls.

outputs.title: Standard SCoP operating model
outputs.summary: A clear and reusable model defining how Strategic Communities of Practice are established, led, supported, operated, reviewed, renewed and, where necessary, closed.
acceptanceCriteria: The model defines the responsibilities of convenors, members, the central support function and the governing committee.
The model sets expectations for participation, communication, collaboration and decision-making.
The relationship between community activity and institutional education priorities is clear.
The model is approved through the agreed senior education governance route by December 2026.

outputs.title: SCoP resourcing and eligible-use framework
outputs.summary: An agreed framework defining the indicative resource available to communities, the balance between convenor support, community activity and funded projects, and the purposes for which SCoP funding may be used.
acceptanceCriteria: The indicative resource envelope and its principal components are defined.
Eligible and ineligible uses of funding are clear, including support for purposeful activity, collaboration, inquiry, dissemination and institutional change.
Budget ownership, authorisation, monitoring and reporting arrangements are documented.
The framework is sufficiently clear to inform the first convenor and community-project calls.

outputs.title: SCoP governance and accountability framework
outputs.owner: Mark Peace with senior education governance sponsor
outputs.summary: A defined route through which communities agree plans and priorities, report on activity and expenditure, demonstrate progress and impact, and receive challenge, support and decisions about continuation or change.
acceptanceCriteria: The Innovation Committee's remit, membership, delegated authority and reporting route are agreed.
The process through which communities agree and report their plans, priorities and expenditure is defined.
Annual review, renewal, escalation and closure arrangements are documented.
The relationship between the Innovation Committee and existing education governance is clear.

outputs.title: Minimum expectations for SCoP activity, output and impact
outputs.summary: A proportionate baseline defining what every Strategic Community of Practice is expected to do and demonstrate while allowing communities to respond differently to their subject matter.
acceptanceCriteria: Minimum expectations cover a visible programme of activity, sustained participation and exchange or development of practice.
Communities are expected to create tangible outputs, recommendations, resources, collaborations or other appropriate products.
Communities are expected to demonstrate evidence of influence on education, policy, practice or institutional decision-making.
A proportionate annual account of activity, learning, expenditure, outputs and impact is required.

outputs.title: Workload-release and backfill proposition
outputs.owner: Mark Peace with faculty education leadership
outputs.summary: A credible institutional proposition for workload release, workload allocation or backfill for SCoP convenors and colleagues leading funded community projects.
acceptanceCriteria: Eligibility, indicative scale and duration of support are defined.
The relationship between central funding, faculty contribution and local workload arrangements is set out.
Approval, recording and review arrangements are defined.
Faculty positions are sufficiently clear to make a credible and equitable offer in the first funded calls, with any wider unresolved workload-policy questions routed separately.

outputs.title: King's Academy ownership and support model
outputs.summary: A phased model through which a named King's Academy Portfolio Lead takes increasing ownership from Mark Peace, supported by permanent portfolio administration and coordination as convenors and projects change.
acceptanceCriteria: A named King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead, or an agreed appointment route, is confirmed.
Responsibilities and decision rights are clear across the Portfolio Lead, Portfolio Coordinator, individual convenors, project leads and the Innovation Committee.
A phased transfer of portfolio ownership from Mark Peace to King's Academy is agreed.
Initial permanent administrative capacity of 0.2 FTE is confirmed, with scaling assumptions for the three- and six-community portfolio.
The recurrent workload-release or backfill requirement for the Portfolio Lead is identified and an agreed route to quantification and funding is recorded.

existingCapacity.role: Step owner and substantive design lead
existingCapacity.contribution: Lead the proposition, develop the operating model, convene the institutional discussions, resolve substantive policy choices and secure approval.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The work would lack substantive leadership and a clear route from consultation to an agreed institutional model.

existingCapacity.role: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead design and shadowing capacity
existingCapacity.contribution: Identify a colleague to work alongside Mark Peace, contribute communities-of-practice expertise, learn from the prototype and prepare for the progressive transfer of portfolio ownership.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Permanent institutional ownership would remain unclear and operational responsibility could remain with Mark Peace by default.

existingCapacity.contribution: Develop and communicate faculty positions on workload allocation, release, backfill, faculty contribution and the local operation of convenor and project roles.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The first calls could make an offer that faculties cannot implement consistently or fairly.

existingCapacity.contribution: Define the resource envelope, eligible expenditure, budget ownership, approval routes, monitoring and reporting arrangements.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The proposed funding model may be unaffordable, difficult to administer or insufficiently controlled.

existingCapacity.contribution: Advise on workable approaches to workload release, workload allocation and backfill for convenors and funded project leads.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The workload proposition may not be implementable through existing employment and faculty processes.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide the decision route for the operating model and establish the Innovation Committee's remit, authority and relationship with existing education governance.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The model and committee could be established without sufficient authority or accountability.

newInvestment.rationale: Provides 0.1 FTE of time-limited project control and coordination through development of the operating model, the first calls and mobilisation of the first funded cycle. This capacity is temporary and does not transfer into business as usual.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The work may remain a series of useful conversations without sufficient coordination, decision tracking and follow-through to implement the model.

newInvestment.item: King's Academy SCoP Project Support Officer and Portfolio Coordinator
newInvestment.rationale: Provides an initial 0.2 FTE of permanent administrative and coordinating capacity in King's Academy. During mobilisation the role supports meetings, records, consultation, communications, calls and process design; in business as usual it maintains committee support, annual processes, records, onboarding, reporting and continuity as convenors change.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Detailed administration would fall to the substantive lead and no permanent operational capacity or institutional memory would be established for the portfolio.

enablingConditions.condition: King's Academy identifies a prospective SCoP Portfolio Lead and protects approximately 0.1 FTE for design and shadowing during Step 2.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Early in the September-December 2026 design period
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The operating model would be designed without the future institutional owner and the transfer from Mark Peace would be delayed.

enablingConditions.condition: Faculties nominate participants with sufficient authority to develop and communicate positions on workload release, backfill and faculty contribution.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before the workload proposition is finalised
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Consultation may produce views but not positions that can support a credible institutional offer.

enablingConditions.condition: Finance, HR and faculty operations participate early enough to shape the model rather than being asked to approve a completed proposal.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: During the first phase of model design
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Late operational objections could delay approval or require substantial redesign.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm the senior governance route that will approve the operating model and establish the Innovation Committee with sufficient delegated authority.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The model may be agreed informally without an authoritative decision or effective accountability route.

enablingConditions.condition: Agree a route to quantify and fund the recurrent King's Academy workload-release or backfill requirement as the Portfolio Lead assumes permanent ownership.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before substantive ownership transfers from Mark Peace
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The transfer may depend on unprotected goodwill and become unsustainable as the portfolio expands.

risks.title: Faculties do not reach a sufficiently clear workload position
risks.mitigation: Develop a workable proposition for the first calls, record faculty positions and exceptions, and route any wider institutional workload-policy questions separately rather than requiring them to be resolved within this step.

risks.title: Permanent ownership remains with Mark Peace by default
risks.mitigation: Identify the King's Academy Portfolio Lead during Step 2, agree a phased transfer of responsibility and record the associated workload-release or backfill requirement.

risks.title: Permanent administrative capacity is treated as temporary project support
risks.mitigation: Record the initial 0.2 FTE Portfolio Coordinator as recurrent King's Academy capacity from the outset, with explicit assumptions about how it may need to scale as the portfolio grows.

risks.title: The operating model is either too vague or too prescriptive
risks.mitigation: Define firm minimum expectations, decision rights and financial controls while allowing each community flexibility over its substantive programme, outputs and routes to impact.

risks.title: The Innovation Committee is established without sufficient authority
risks.mitigation: Agree its remit, delegated decisions, reporting route and relationship with existing education governance before the operating model is approved.

steps.title: Confirm interim convenors and integrate the remaining communities
steps.summary: During September and October 2026, identify existing institutional leaders to act as interim, unremitted convenors while the Experiential Learning Community completes its launch and the common governance and support model continues to develop. Use their leadership to engage the AI in Education and Inclusive Education constituencies and bring both communities into the shared institutional frame by the end of October.

outputs.title: Three communities operating in a common frame
outputs.summary: By the end of October, Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education each have interim leadership, a founding constituency and an initial programme of activity.

steps.title: Run the first funded convenor and community-project calls
steps.summary: From January to April 2027, run coordinated calls for funded Community Convenors and community-aligned projects. Complete assessment and selection by April so that successful convenors, faculty release and backfill arrangements, project leads and funding can be confirmed and mobilised for a September start.

outputs.title: Completed institutional calls
outputs.summary: Convenors and projects selected through clear eligibility, support, assessment and decision arrangements.

outputs.title: Selected funded leadership and project portfolio
outputs.summary: Successful convenors and projects identified for appointment and commencement in September 2027.

steps.title: Build the first three communities and establish their operating conventions
steps.summary: From November 2026 to June 2027, develop the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities under interim leadership into active and recognisable communities of practice. Begin this work as soon as all three communities are operating in the shared institutional frame, alongside finalisation of the common governance and support model. Through their early work, establish and test shared conventions for convenorship, participation, communication, collaborative inquiry, student and partner involvement, funded activity, decision-making and routes into institutional influence.

outputs.title: Three established communities with shared operating conventions
outputs.summary: Three communities with interim leadership, sustained participation and credible programmes of activity, alongside an agreed and tested set of conventions to guide future communities of practice.

steps.title: Confirm appointments and mobilise the first funded cycle
steps.summary: From May to August 2027, confirm the selected convenors and projects, finalise faculty release, workload allocation, backfill, budgets and delivery arrangements, and manage the handover from interim leadership. Prepare the three communities, funded convenors and project teams to begin the first funded operating cycle in September.

outputs.title: Confirmed funded appointments and projects
outputs.summary: Convenors, project leads, budgets, workload arrangements and expectations confirmed for September commencement.

outputs.title: First funded cycle ready to operate
outputs.summary: The three communities and their funded activity are mobilised for the 2027-28 academic year.

steps.title: Review the initial mobilisation, agree the expansion portfolio and launch the 2028-29 calls
steps.summary: During July and August 2027, review and report on the initial community-building phase as soon as it concludes. Assess establishment, participation, governance, interim convenorship, faculty support, project mechanisms and emerging institutional influence; refine the model; agree the three additional strategic communities to be developed for 2028-29; and launch the associated convenor and community-project calls by the end of August.

outputs.title: Initial mobilisation review
outputs.summary: An evidence-led assessment of whether the first three communities and their shared operating model have been successfully established.

outputs.title: Approved six-community portfolio
outputs.summary: Three additional strategic communities agreed for development and funded operation in the 2028-29 academic year.

outputs.title: Open 2028-29 convenor and project calls
outputs.summary: Calls launched by the end of August for renewed and new convenors and community-aligned projects across the approved six-community portfolio.

steps.title: Operate the first funded three-community cycle
steps.summary: Operate the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities through the September 2027-June 2028 academic-year cycle. Support their funded convenors, programmes, projects, participation and routes into institutional influence while gathering consistent evidence of activity, outcomes and resource requirements.

outputs.title: First funded operating cycle
outputs.summary: Three communities complete a coherent September-June cycle with funded leadership, visible activity and evidence of their contribution.

steps.title: Complete selection for the expanded portfolio
steps.summary: During September and October 2027, assess the 2028-29 convenor and community-project calls launched following the initial mobilisation review. Complete selection by the end of October, covering renewals, new appointments and the three additional communities, so that the expanded portfolio can move directly into mobilisation from November.

outputs.title: Selected 2028-29 convenors and projects
outputs.summary: Renewed and new convenors and a funded project portfolio selected for the six-community operating cycle beginning in September 2028.

steps.title: Mobilise the expanded six-community portfolio
steps.summary: From November 2027 to August 2028, confirm appointments, faculty release, workload allocation, backfill, budgets and project delivery arrangements. Establish the three additional communities, build their founding memberships and priorities, and prepare all six communities, convenors and funded projects to begin the next operating cycle together in September.

outputs.title: Expanded portfolio ready to operate
outputs.summary: All six communities, their funded convenors and their selected projects are mobilised for September 2028.

steps.title: Review the first funded operating cycle, refine the model and launch the 2029-30 calls
steps.summary: During July and August 2028, review and report on the completed September-June operating cycle. Assess participation, activity, impact, governance, convenorship, faculty release and backfill, funding, project mechanisms and institutional influence; refine the model for the expanded portfolio; and launch the 2029-30 convenor and community-project calls by the end of August.

outputs.title: First funded-cycle impact and operating-model review
outputs.summary: An assessment of the first funded cycle with agreed refinements to governance, resourcing and operating arrangements for the expanded portfolio.

outputs.title: Open 2029-30 convenor and project calls
outputs.summary: Calls launched by the end of August for the next annual portfolio of convenors and community-aligned projects.

steps.title: Operate the six-community portfolio
steps.summary: Operate all six strategic communities through the September 2028-June 2029 academic-year cycle, supporting their funded convenors, programmes, projects, institutional influence and cross-community learning while gathering consistent evidence of participation, outcomes and resource requirements.

outputs.title: Full six-community operating cycle
outputs.summary: Six communities complete a coherent September-June cycle, including the contribution of their funded projects.

steps.title: Complete 2029-30 selection and develop the BAU settlement
steps.summary: During September and October 2028, assess the 2029-30 convenor and community-project calls and complete selection by the end of October for a September start. In parallel, develop the proposed permanent institutional ownership, governance route, budget holding, recurrent resource settlement and annual planning arrangements required for business as usual.

outputs.title: Selected 2029-30 portfolio
outputs.summary: Convenors and projects selected for the operating cycle beginning in September 2029.

outputs.title: Proposed BAU resource and governance settlement
outputs.summary: A developed proposal for permanent ownership, governance, recurrent resources and the continuing annual commissioning rhythm.

steps.title: Mobilise the 2029-30 portfolio and prepare the institutional handover
steps.summary: From November 2028 to August 2029, confirm appointments, faculty release, backfill, budgets and project delivery arrangements for the 2029-30 portfolio. Prepare the transfer of governance, reporting, operational support, budgets and accountability from mobilisation to the proposed permanent institutional owner.

outputs.title: Portfolio mobilised and handover prepared
outputs.summary: The next annual portfolio is mobilised for September and the operational, governance and resource arrangements are ready to transfer once the permanent model is approved in August.

steps.title: Review the six-community cycle and confirm the permanent model
steps.summary: During July and August 2029, review and report on the completed six-community operating cycle. Assess impact and sustainability, determine which communities should continue or evolve, and approve the permanent institutional owner, governance arrangements, recurrent resource settlement and annual planning cycle by the end of August.

outputs.title: Six-community impact and sustainability review
outputs.summary: A completed assessment of the expanded portfolio and its contribution after a full operating cycle.

outputs.title: Approved permanent institutional model
outputs.summary: Permanent ownership, governance, recurrent resources and the annual commissioning and operating rhythm confirmed by the end of August 2029.

steps.title: Transition to business as usual
steps.summary: From September 2029, complete the transfer to the permanent institutional owner so that Strategic Communities of Practice continue through the established rhythm of September-June operation, July-August review, reporting and call launch, September-October selection and November-August mobilisation.

outputs.title: Business-as-usual transition complete
outputs.summary: Strategic Communities of Practice operate through permanent ownership, governance, recurrent resources and an established annual planning cycle from September 2029.
